selected_hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering white cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours typically depart from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town and include stops at the Blue Caves.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, herbs, and spices. Join a guided street food tour to sample spanakopita, loukoumades (honey donuts), souvlaki, and fresh Greek yogurt with honey. A deeply authentic culinary experience loved by locals.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand caused by crushed coral and its shallow, crystal-clear lagoon waters. You can wade across to the small island of Elafonissi. Rent a sunbed and umbrella, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and enjoy the unspoiled natural beauty of one of Europe's best beaches.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a local Cretan home or taverna where you'll learn to prepare traditional dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and kalitsounia (cheese pastries). The class typically includes a visit to a local market or olive grove, and you'll sit down to enjoy the meal you've prepared with local wine or raki.

experiences.name: Sunset Dinner at a Clifftop Taverna in Oia
experiences.description: Experience the world-famous Santorini sunset from the village of Oia while dining at a traditional clifftop taverna. Enjoy fresh grilled octopus, fava (yellow split pea puree), fresh catch of the day, and local Assyrtiko white wine as the sun dips below the caldera. Book a table in advance to secure the best view and arrive early to explore the charming blue-domed village.

weather.summary: Hot and sunny. Sea warm enough for swimming.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the airport, clear customs, and arrange transport to Navagio Beach area (ferry or taxi). Check in to the Boutique Stay and freshen up. Take a relaxed first look at the stunning surroundings near Navagio (Shipwreck Beach) viewpoint — the iconic clifftop panorama is free and just minutes from the accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the nearby port village of Porto Vromi. Enjoy the sunset over the Ionian Sea from a clifftop vantage point. Settle into the local pace of life.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport before landing
meals.lunch: Pick up a budget gyros wrap or spanakopita from a local bakery near the port (€3–5)
meals.dinner: Taverna Navagio or a local family-run taverna near Porto Vromi — try grilled sardines and Greek salad (€10–14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some euros at the airport or use an ATM. Keep coins handy for small vendors. Ferry to Navagio beach viewpoint area may require a short drive or taxi (~€10–15). Rest well — big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Early morning boat trip to Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach — one of Greece's most iconic beaches. Arrive before crowds for the best experience. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water and explore the famous shipwreck. Boat trips depart from Porto Vromi and cost approximately €10–15 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Navagio and relax on a quieter nearby cove beach. Try Xigia Sulfur Beach, a short drive away, where natural sulfur springs mix with the sea — unique and free to access.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the village of Anafonitria (closest inland village) for a quiet evening walk. Visit the 15th-century Monastery of Anafonitria — free to enter and historically significant.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and fruit from a local mini-market (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic to take on the boat — bread, local cheese (graviera), olives, and tomatoes from a mini-market (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Local taverna in Anafonitria village — try moussaka or stuffed tomatoes (gemista) with house wine (€10–13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bring reef-safe sunscreen, water, and a hat. Navagio is exposed with no shade — arrive early. Boat tickets can be booked the evening before at Porto Vromi dock to save time.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or ATV (€15–25/day) and explore the northern tip of Zakynthos. Head to the Blue Caves near Cape Skinari — stunning sea caves with electric-blue water caused by light refraction. Boat tours from Skinari cost around €10–12.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue south along the coastal road to Makris Gialos Beach — a quieter, less touristy stretch of sand perfect for swimming. Bring snorkeling gear if you have it.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back and stop at a clifftop viewpoint for golden-hour photos over the Ionian Sea. Return to accommodation and relax.

meals.breakfast: Tiropita (cheese pie) and coffee from a local bakery (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Fresh fish sandwich or grilled octopus from a seaside kiosk near Cape Skinari (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the accommodation using local market ingredients — feta, olives, bread, and cold cuts (€6–8 total)

day_by_day.notes: Scooter/ATV rental requires a valid driving license. Fill up fuel before heading north — petrol stations are sparse. Wear sunscreen and a helmet. Roads are winding but scenic.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Venetian Castle of Bochali above Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) — a short drive south. The castle ruins are free to explore and offer sweeping views over the town and bay. Explore the castle grounds and read about Zakynthos's Venetian history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend into Zakynthos Town and explore Solomos Square, the main plaza named after the national poet Dionysios Solomos. Visit the Museum of Solomos (€3 entry) and wander the elegant arcaded streets. Browse the local market for affordable souvenirs — local honey, olive oil, and nougat (mandolato).
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Zakynthos Town waterfront promenade at sunset. The harbor is lively and beautiful in the evening light.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Zakynthos Town — Greek coffee and kourambiedes (almond cookies) (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Souvlaki pita from a street stall in Zakynthos Town (€3–4)
meals.dinner: Taverna Mesogios or similar waterfront taverna — grilled sea bream with lemon potatoes and a carafe of local white wine (€12–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Zakynthos Town is about 30–40 min drive from Navagio area. Parking is available near the harbor. The town has ATMs, pharmacies, and supermarkets — a good day to stock up on supplies.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning ferry from Zakynthos to Kefalonia (Argostoli port) — ferries run regularly and cost approximately €8–12 per person. Arrive in Argostoli and check out the lively capital. Walk the long stone bridge (Drapano Bridge) across the lagoon — free and scenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Melissani Lake Cave — a stunning underground lake where sunlight pours through a collapsed roof. Entry is around €7. Then head to nearby Drogarati Cave (€5 entry) — an impressive stalactite cavern. Both are within 15 km of Argostoli.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Argostoli and explore the waterfront. Watch the famous Kefalonian loggerhead turtles that often swim near the harbor in the evenings — completely free and magical.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the accommodation before the ferry, or grab a pastry at the Zakynthos port café (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Kefalonian meat pie (kreatopita) from a local bakery in Argostoli — a regional specialty (€3–4)
meals.dinner: Taverna near Argostoli harbor — try Kefalonian lamb stew (stifado) with local Robola wine (€12–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a day trip to Kefalonia — return ferry to Zakynthos in the evening. Check ferry schedules in advance as they can be limited. Alternatively, consider staying a night in Kefalonia if budget allows, but it adds accommodation cost.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day at Gerakas Beach — one of Zakynthos's most beautiful and protected beaches (protected turtle nesting site). The beach is stunning with fine white sand and clear water. No water sports are allowed, keeping it peaceful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the short nature trail above Gerakas for views of the Laganas Bay. Spot loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta) in the water — Zakynthos is one of their main nesting grounds in the Mediterranean.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Laganas village for a livelier evening atmosphere. Browse the market stalls and enjoy the buzz of the most popular resort area on the island.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with local honey and walnuts from the mini-market (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic at the beach — hummus, pita bread, cucumber, and tomatoes (€4–5)
meals.dinner: Taverna in Laganas — grilled chicken souvlaki platter with tzatziki and fries (€9–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Gerakas Beach has strict rules: no umbrellas in the central section (turtle nesting zone), no entry after sunset. Respect the wildlife — it's a protected natural area. Bring your own shade and plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the village of Volimes — the traditional craft and lace-making village in northern Zakynthos. Browse handmade textiles, local honey, and olive products. The village church of Agia Paraskevi is worth a look inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Navagio viewpoint again (5 min from Volimes) for different lighting and photos — the afternoon sun hits the beach differently and creates beautiful colors. Then relax at a quiet cove near Porto Vromi.
day_by_day.evening: Slow Sunday evening — sit at a kafeneion (traditional Greek café) in a local village, order a freddo espresso or ouzo with mezedes, and watch the world go by.

meals.breakfast: Honey and sesame bread rings (koulouri) with local honey purchased in Volimes (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Simple mezedes plate at a village kafeneion — olives, feta, bread, and grilled halloumi (€6–8)
meals.dinner: Home-style cooking at the accommodation — pasta with local olive oil, garlic, and feta (€4–5 total)

day_by_day.notes: Sunday is quieter — many shops may be closed. The village of Volimes is authentic and less touristy. Prices for local products like honey and olive oil are very reasonable when bought directly from producers.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry from Zakynthos to Patras on the mainland (approximately 3 hours, €15–20 per person). Arrive in Patras — Greece's third-largest city and a gateway to the Peloponnese. Drop bags at a budget hostel or guesthouse (€15–25/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Patras Castle (Kastro) — a Byzantine fortress with panoramic views over the city and Gulf of Patras. Free entry. Walk through the historic upper town and the elegant neoclassical streets below.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Patras waterfront (Rio) and enjoy the vibrant café culture. Patras is known for its carnival tradition and lively social scene.

meals.breakfast: Eat before boarding the ferry or grab a tiropita at the Zakynthos port (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Souvlaki wrap from a street stall in Patras city center (€3–4)
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Patras — try local pasta (pastitsio) or grilled octopus with ouzo (€10–13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel day — pack light and keep essentials accessible. Ferry from Zakynthos to Patras departs from Zakynthos Town port. Book tickets in advance online for the cheapest fares. Patras is a transit city but has genuine local character.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus from Patras to Nafplio (approximately 2.5 hours via Corinth, €12–15). Arrive in Nafplio — one of Greece's most beautiful and romantic towns. Check into a budget guesthouse (€20–30/night). Climb the 999 steps to the Palamidi Fortress for stunning views (€4 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming old town of Nafplio — neoclassical mansions, Venetian architecture, and narrow cobblestone streets. Visit Syntagma Square and the small Archaeological Museum (€3 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the waterfront and admire the Bourtzi castle on the small island in the harbor (lit up beautifully at night). Enjoy the relaxed evening atmosphere of Nafplio.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and bougatsa (custard pastry) at Patras bus station before departure (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Souvlaki or gyros pita near Nafplio bus station on arrival (€3–4)
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Nafplio old town — try lamb chops (paidakia) with roasted vegetables and local wine (€12–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Nafplio is a gem of the Peloponnese and very walkable. The Palamidi climb is steep — wear good shoes and go early before the heat peaks. Budget accommodation fills up quickly in June; book ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ancient Epidaurus — one of the best-preserved ancient theatres in the world (UNESCO World Heritage Site). Take a local bus or shared taxi (€5–8 each way). Entry is €12 but includes the Archaeological Museum. The acoustics of the 14,000-seat theatre are extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return, stop at Tolo Beach — a lovely sandy beach near Nafplio with calm, warm water. Swim and relax in the afternoon sun. The beach is free and uncrowded on weekdays.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Nafplio and enjoy a slow evening. Browse the local shops for affordable ceramics and olive wood products. Sit at a waterfront café for a sunset drink.

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and a koulouri from a street vendor in Nafplio (€1–2)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from the market — cheese, bread, olives, and fruit (€4–5)
meals.dinner: Ouzeris (meze restaurant) in Nafplio — shared plates of taramosalata, grilled calamari, and horta (wild greens) with bread (€10–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check local bus schedules to Epidaurus the evening before — they can be infrequent. Epidaurus sometimes hosts evening performances in summer (Greek drama festival); check if any coincide with your visit — tickets from €15 are a worthwhile splurge.

day_by_day.morning: Take a bus from Nafplio to Athens (approximately 2.5 hours, €13–16). Arrive at Athens KTEL Kifissou bus terminal and take the metro to central Athens (€1.20). Check into a budget hostel in Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood (€18–28/night). Head straight to the Acropolis — arrive before noon to beat the worst heat (entry €20, or free with EU student card).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Acropolis Museum (€10 entry) — world-class exhibits in a stunning modern building. Then wander through the Plaka neighborhood — Athens's oldest district with charming streets, neoclassical houses, and small squares.
day_by_day.evening: Climb Filopappou Hill (free) for the best sunset view of the Acropolis — photographers' favorite spot. Descend to Monastiraki Square for the lively evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and tiropita at a Nafplio bakery before the bus (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Street food in Monastiraki — souvlaki wrap from Kostas or Thanasis (legendary budget spots, €2.50–3.50)
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Psiri neighborhood — try fasolada (bean soup) and fried cod with skordalia (garlic dip) (€9–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Athens is hot in June — carry water everywhere. The Acropolis is best visited in the morning or late afternoon. Combo tickets covering multiple archaeological sites (€30) offer good value if you plan to visit several. Metro is cheap and efficient.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ancient Agora of Athens (€10, or included in combo ticket) — the marketplace and civic center of ancient Athens, with the beautifully preserved Temple of Hephaestus. Then explore Kerameikos Archaeological Site (€8) — Athens's ancient cemetery, less crowded and genuinely atmospheric.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the metro to Piraeus (€1.20) and catch a ferry to the nearby Saronic island of Aegina (approximately 1 hour, €8–10 each way). Visit the stunning Temple of Aphaia (€6) and swim at one of Aegina's beaches. Return ferry to Piraeus in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Athens, explore the vibrant Exarchia neighborhood — bohemian, artsy, and very local. Browse independent bookshops and street art. Enjoy Athens's famous nightlife culture (Greeks eat dinner late — 9–10 PM is normal).

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or grab a spanakopita and coffee from a nearby bakery (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish or pistachio ice cream (Aegina is famous for pistachios!) on the island (€6–10)
meals.dinner: Mezedopolio (meze taverna) in Exarchia — shared small plates: dolmades, saganaki, and grilled vegetables with wine (€10–13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Aegina is a perfect quick island escape from Athens. Pistachios from Aegina are world-famous — buy a bag to take home as an affordable, authentic souvenir. Check the last ferry back to Piraeus before you go.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — visit the Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) for a vivid, authentic Greek market experience. Browse the fish, meat, spice, and olive stalls. Buy local products to take home — olive oil, dried herbs, honey, or local cheeses at market prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute sightseeing — walk up Lycabettus Hill (free, or take the funicular for €7 return) for 360° views over Athens and the Acropolis. Visit the Benaki Museum (€9) if time allows — excellent collection of Greek art and culture across the ages.
day_by_day.evening: Final Greek dinner in Athens. Head to Monastiraki or Thissio for a meal with a view of the illuminated Acropolis. Raise a glass of ouzo or local wine to a wonderful 13-day Greek adventure.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at a café near the market — eggs, feta, olives, bread, and tomatoes (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Central Market area — fresh fruit, cheese, and bread from the stalls (€4–5)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly for the final night — rooftop taverna in Monastiraki with Acropolis views — grilled lamb chops, Greek salad, and a bottle of Assyrtiko white wine (€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep track of your departure logistics — Athens airport (ATH) is about 40 min from the city center by metro (€9 one way). If flying out the next morning, consider an early night. Store luggage at the hostel if your flight is late. Greece will leave you wanting to return — it always does!

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage and arrange transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from airport to Navagio Beach boutique stay (~1.5 hours). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the nearby clifftop viewpoint overlooking the iconic Shipwreck Beach (Navagio) to soak in the first stunning views of the turquoise cove below.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the hotel and explore the immediate surroundings. Head to a nearby taverna in the Anafonitria village area for a relaxed welcome dinner.

meals.breakfast: Snack at the airport before landing
meals.lunch: Light bite or snack at a café near the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Taverna Navagio or a local village taverna in Anafonitria — try grilled octopus, Greek salad, and local white wine (budget ~€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Prioritize rest after travel. Confirm boat tour bookings for Navagio Beach with hotel reception.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning boat trip to Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach — the most famous beach in Greece. Arrive before the crowds (~9:00 AM) to swim in the crystal-clear turquoise water beside the rusted shipwreck. Snorkeling gear available for rent on the boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from Navagio by midday. Relax at the hotel pool or explore the Blue Caves on the northern tip of Zakynthos via a short boat extension from the same tour operator — stunning sea arches and vivid blue water reflections.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or taxi to the village of Volimes, the nearest traditional village, known for local honey, nougat, and handmade goods. Browse the small market stalls before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery — fresh tiropita (cheese pie) and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Packed snack or light mezedes at a seaside kiosk near the boat dock
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Volimes village — lamb kleftiko, horiatiki salad, and local Zakynthian wine (budget ~€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Navagio boat tour in advance — morning departures fill up fast in June. Wear reef-safe sunscreen; water shoes are helpful on the pebble beach.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Porto Vromi Cove, a sheltered natural harbor a short drive from Navagio. Rent a small paddleboat or kayak to explore the hidden sea caves along the coastline at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head south to Agios Nikolaos Beach on the west coast — a quieter, less-visited beach with golden sand and calm waters perfect for swimming. Bring a picnic or grab snacks from a nearby kiosk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel area. Sunset cocktails at the clifftop viewpoint above Navagio — one of the best sunset spots in all of Greece. Then dinner at the hotel restaurant or a nearby spot.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — yogurt with local honey, fruit, and eggs
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch with local bread, olives, feta, and cold cuts from a village deli (budget ~€8–12 per person)
meals.dinner: Boutique hotel restaurant or a nearby clifftop eatery — fresh sea bream, tzatziki, and local rosé wine (budget ~€25–32 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Porto Vromi is also a departure point for Navagio boat tours — a good backup if Day 2 weather was poor. Kayak rentals typically cost €10–15/hour.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Zakynthos Town (Zante Town) — the island's capital, about 40 minutes by car or bus. Visit the Byzantine Museum housing post-Byzantine icons rescued after the 1953 earthquake, and stroll through Solomos Square.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Venetian Castle (Kastro) perched above Zakynthos Town for panoramic views of the island and Ionian Sea. Walk through the charming arcaded streets lined with neoclassical buildings rebuilt after the earthquake.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Zakynthos Town at a harborfront restaurant. The port area has a great mix of authentic tavernas and lively atmosphere. Return to hotel by taxi or rental car.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional ouzeri in Zakynthos Town — ouzo, grilled sardines, and mezedes (budget ~€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Harborfront taverna in Zakynthos Town — pastitsada (local pasta with rooster), fresh calamari, and local wine (budget ~€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Byzantine Museum is closed on Mondays — check the day of the week and adjust accordingly. Bus from the north of the island runs a few times daily; a rental car gives more flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Myzithres Rock formations on the southwest coast — dramatic twin limestone sea stacks rising from the water. Accessible via a short hike down a coastal path with spectacular views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Limnionas Beach, a hidden gem on the west coast with emerald-green water carved into the cliffs. Swim directly from the rocks in calm, sheltered conditions. Very few tourists visit this spot.
day_by_day.evening: Back at the hotel. Enjoy a quiet evening — perhaps a spa treatment at the boutique hotel (if available) or a peaceful dinner with wine on a terrace.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at a local café — Greek yogurt parfait and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Small taverna near Limnionas — grilled fish of the day and village salad (budget ~€18–24 per person)
meals.dinner: Hotel terrace dinner or nearby hillside restaurant — slow-roasted lamb, roasted vegetables, and local wine (budget ~€24–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Limnionas is best visited on calm days — the narrow access road requires a small car. Myzithres is best viewed from the clifftop path rather than the water.

day_by_day.morning: Ferry from Zakynthos port to Kefalonia (Argostoli or Pessada port) — approximately 1–1.5 hours. An easy island-hop that opens up a second beautiful Ionian island. Settle into a mid-range guesthouse in Argostoli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Argostoli, Kefalonia's charming capital. Visit the Drapano Bridge (De Bosset Bridge), the longest stone bridge over the sea in Greece. Walk along the lively waterfront promenade and watch the loggerhead sea turtles that frequent the harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Argostoli's town center — lively atmosphere with a range of authentic restaurants and cafés.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before ferry departure
meals.lunch: Lunch in Argostoli after arrival — try a local bakery or café for spanakopita and fresh juice (budget ~€10–14 per person)
meals.dinner: Waterfront restaurant in Argostoli — Kefalonian meat pie (kreatopita), fresh grilled fish, and local Robola white wine (budget ~€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Zakynthos–Kefalonia ferry in advance for June. Ferries run from Pessada (south Zakynthos) to Agios Nikolaos (south Kefalonia) — a rental car makes this transition smoother.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Melissani Cave — a stunning underground lake inside a collapsed cave where the turquoise water glows in the sunlight. Boat ride through the cave with a guide. Arrive early to avoid long queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Myrtos Beach — consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in Europe. Dramatic white pebbles, sheer white cliffs, and impossibly blue water. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the spectacular scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the hilltop village of Assos — a tiny, picturesque Venetian village on a peninsula with a ruined castle. Perfect for a golden-hour walk and dinner at a small local taverna.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or a café in Argostoli
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar at Myrtos — sandwiches and cold drinks (budget ~€10–15 per person)
meals.dinner: Taverna in Assos village — stuffed tomatoes, grilled octopus, and local wine overlooking the bay (budget ~€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Melissani Cave opens at 9:00 AM — arrive by 9:15 AM to beat tour groups. Myrtos has limited shade; bring an umbrella. The road to Myrtos is winding — drive carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Fiskardo, the only village in Kefalonia that survived the 1953 earthquake, retaining its original Venetian architecture. Stroll the colorful harbor lined with pastel buildings, boutique shops, and fishing boats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a boat trip from Fiskardo to Ithaca island (day trip, ~30 minutes by water taxi or small ferry). Visit the Cave of the Nymphs and the Archaeological Museum of Vathy — small but fascinating connections to Homer's Odyssey.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fiskardo by early evening. Dinner at one of the upscale-casual harborfront restaurants before driving back to Argostoli.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Argostoli before driving north
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Vathy, Ithaca — fresh fish soup and bread at a harbor café (budget ~€14–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Fiskardo harbor restaurant — lobster pasta or grilled sea bass, local wine (budget ~€28–35 per person — slightly splurge-worthy setting)

day_by_day.notes: Water taxis from Fiskardo to Ithaca are informal — ask at the harbor. Confirm return times before booking. Fiskardo is the most upscale village on Kefalonia; prices reflect this.

day_by_day.morning: Ferry from Kefalonia to Patras on the mainland (approximately 3 hours), then drive or take a bus south to the Peloponnese. Head toward the coastal town of Nafplio — one of Greece's most romantic towns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Nafplio by early afternoon. Check into a mid-range boutique hotel in the old town. Explore the narrow, bougainvillea-draped streets of the Venetian old town and visit Syntagma Square.
day_by_day.evening: Climb the 999 steps (or take the road) to the magnificent Palamidi Fortress for sweeping views over the Argolic Gulf at sunset. Dinner in the old town afterward.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the ferry
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry or a quick bite upon arrival in Nafplio — gyros wrap from a local souvlaki spot (budget ~€8–12 per person)
meals.dinner: Old town restaurant in Nafplio — moussaka, dakos salad, and local Peloponnese wine (budget ~€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a longer travel day — start early. The Patras–Nafplio drive is about 2.5 hours. Alternatively, fly Kefalonia–Athens and drive to Nafplio (2 hours) for a faster connection.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Mycenae — the legendary Bronze Age citadel, just 45 minutes from Nafplio. Visit the Lion Gate, the Treasury of Atreus (Tomb of Agamemnon), and the archaeological museum on-site. A UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio. Spend the afternoon at Arvanitia Beach, a small rocky beach just below the town walls — perfect for a refreshing swim in the warm Argolic Gulf. Alternatively, take the short boat ride to Bourtzi Castle in the harbor.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Nafplio's vibrant restaurant scene. The old town comes alive in the evening with locals and visitors dining al fresco.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery — bougatsa (custard pastry) and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Taverna near Mycenae site — simple village lunch of grilled meats and salad (budget ~€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Nafplio old town restaurant — fresh seafood mezedes, grilled prawns, and local wine (budget ~€24–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Mycenae opens at 8:00 AM — visit early before the heat peaks. Entry is approximately €12 per person. Bring water and a hat for the exposed archaeological site.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Epidaurus Ancient Theatre (~30 minutes from Nafplio) — one of the best-preserved ancient theatres in the world, famous for its extraordinary acoustics. Walk the stage and test the acoustics yourself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south to the coastal village of Tolo or Porto Heli — beautiful sandy beaches with calm, warm water. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Nafplio for a final evening in the Peloponnese. Browse the local shops for olive oil, local honey, and ceramics as souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Beachside taverna in Tolo — grilled fish, tzatziki, and cold beer (budget ~€18–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Nafplio waterfront restaurant — slow-cooked lamb chops, roasted peppers, and local wine (budget ~€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Epidaurus hosts a famous summer theatre festival (Hellenic Festival) in June–August — check if a performance coincides with your visit for an unforgettable evening event.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Nafplio to Athens (~2 hours). Check into a mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Koukaki neighborhood — both excellent bases for exploring the city. Drop luggage and head out immediately.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon — the crown jewel of Athens. Arrive by 2:00 PM to avoid the worst midday heat (though June afternoons are still warm). The Acropolis Museum at the base is world-class and air-conditioned.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Monastiraki flea market area and Plaka neighborhood — Athens' charming old quarter. Rooftop bar drinks with Acropolis views before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café stop on the drive or upon arrival in Athens — Greek coffee and a koulouri (sesame bread ring)
meals.lunch: Mezedopoleio (mezedes restaurant) in Monastiraki — shared plates of dips, grilled halloumi, and dolmades (budget ~€16–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant in Monastiraki with Acropolis views — souvlaki platter, Greek salad, and local beer or wine (budget ~€24–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets online in advance — June queues can be very long. Combined ticket covers multiple Athens archaeological sites. Wear comfortable shoes for the uneven stone paths.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — visit the Central Market (Varvakios Agora) to experience the vibrant sights, sounds, and smells of a traditional Greek market. Pick up last-minute food souvenirs: olive oil, dried herbs, local honey, and spices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: visit the National Archaeological Museum (one of the world's great museums) or stroll through the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood and enjoy a final Greek coffee at a pavement café. Head to the airport with ample time.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — fly home with wonderful memories of beaches, food, history, and the warmth of Greek hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast at a café near the hotel — fresh orange juice, eggs, feta, olives, and village bread
meals.lunch: Quick souvlaki or gyros wrap near the market — the best fast food in Greece (budget ~€8–12 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight — or a final sit-down meal if time allows before departure

day_by_day.notes: Athens airport (ATH) is about 35–40 minutes from the city center by Metro (Line 3, blue line) — affordable, fast, and reliable. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Navagio Beach, Zakynthos Island Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zakynthos International Airport at 13:00. Private transfer arranged to Boutique Stay at Navagio Beach. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome glass of chilled Assyrtiko wine on your private terrace overlooking the Ionian Sea. Take a leisurely stroll along the clifftops above Navagio (Shipwreck Beach) to soak in the iconic views at golden hour.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the resort ambiance with a sunset cocktail at the hotel's clifftop bar. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the boutique hotel's in-house fine dining restaurant featuring fresh Zakynthian seafood and locally sourced produce.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light mezze and chilled white wine at the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: In-house hotel restaurant – grilled whole sea bream with capers, lemon-herb risotto, and local Verdea wine

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer should be pre-booked. Request early check-in if possible. The hotel concierge can arrange a welcome amenity basket with local honey, olive oil, and Zakynthian pastries.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat charter departing from the hotel's nearby dock for an exclusive morning visit to Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach. Arrive before the day-trip crowds for a truly private experience on the iconic white-pebble cove. Swim in the electric-blue waters and explore the rusting hulk of the MV Panagiotis shipwreck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat excursion to the Blue Caves on the northern tip of Zakynthos. Snorkel through the sea arches where sunlight refracts into dazzling blue hues. The private captain can anchor in a secluded cove for a catered onboard lunch with chilled rosé.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel by late afternoon. Enjoy a private in-villa outdoor shower and relax on your terrace. Head to a nearby clifftop taverna in the Anafonitria village for a traditional Zakynthian dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at the hotel – fresh pastries, local honey, yogurt with Zakynthian figs, eggs, and cold cuts
meals.lunch: Catered onboard lunch on the private boat – smoked salmon, Greek salad, stuffed vine leaves, local cheeses, and chilled Malagousia wine
meals.dinner: Clifftop taverna in Anafonitria – slow-braised rabbit stifado, handmade pasta with lobster, and local barrel wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter well in advance through the hotel concierge. Morning departure (8:00–9:00) is strongly recommended to beat tour boats. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, snorkeling gear (or rent premium gear through the hotel), and a hat.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided hike along the dramatic Zakynthian clifftop trails above Navagio Beach. A local expert naturalist guide will lead you through the wild thyme and maquis shrubland, pointing out endemic flora and the best secret viewpoints. End at a panoramic lookout platform for sunrise photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south by private car to the secluded Porto Vromi cove. Rent a small motorized dinghy from the marina to explore hidden sea caves and turquoise lagoons at your own pace. Swim and sunbathe at a quiet beach unreachable by road.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a spa treatment – book a traditional Greek olive oil massage or Aegean sea-salt scrub at the hotel's wellness center. Dinner at a highly regarded seafood restaurant in the nearby village.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – fresh-squeezed orange juice, Greek yogurt parfait, smoked trout, village bread with thyme honey
meals.lunch: Picnic hamper prepared by the hotel chef – artisan sandwiches, marinated octopus salad, fresh fruit, and sparkling water enjoyed on the beach
meals.dinner: Upscale seafood restaurant near Porto Vromi – grilled calamari stuffed with feta and herbs, whole lobster with garlic butter, local Robola white wine

day_by_day.notes: The clifftop hike is approximately 4–5 km and takes about 2 hours at a leisurely pace. Wear sturdy footwear and carry water. The hotel concierge can arrange the private naturalist guide. Spa treatments should be booked 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class hosted by a local Zakynthian chef at a traditional farmhouse near Volimes village. Learn to prepare authentic island dishes: pastitsada (spiced meat pasta), skordalia (garlic dip), and mandolato (nougat with almonds and honey). Tour the herb garden and olive grove.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the historic village of Volimes, known for its handcrafted lace, honey, and local liqueurs. Browse artisan shops and pick up premium souvenirs – Zakynthian honey, handmade ceramics, and local olive oil. Stop at a family-run winery for a private tasting of indigenous Verdea and Avgoustiatis wines.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails back at the hotel's clifftop terrace. Enjoy a leisurely private dinner in your villa or suite with a specially curated menu prepared by the hotel chef – a personalized in-villa dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – continental spread with local pastries, fresh fruit platter, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during the cooking class enjoyed together at the farmhouse table with local wine
meals.dinner: Private in-villa dining – chilled gazpacho, grilled swordfish with caponata, baklava with vanilla ice cream, and a bottle of premium Santorini Assyrtiko

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class runs approximately 3–4 hours including the meal. Confirm dietary restrictions with the farmhouse host in advance. The winery visit should be pre-arranged through the hotel concierge for a private rather than group tasting experience.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning private speedboat transfer from Zakynthos to Kefalonia island (approximately 1.5 hours). Arrive at Fiskardo, the island's most elegant and well-preserved Venetian harbor village. Check into a luxury boutique hotel or villa for a 2-night stay. Stroll around the picturesque harbor lined with pastel-colored mansions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat excursion to the famous Myrtos Beach – consistently ranked among Europe's most beautiful beaches. The dramatic white pebble beach framed by towering limestone cliffs and turquoise water is best enjoyed with your own private boat anchor just offshore. Swim, snorkel, and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fiskardo for dinner at one of the harbor's finest restaurants. Watch the superyachts drift in as you dine on fresh Kefalonian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at Zakynthos hotel before departure – pastries, fruit, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic on the boat at Myrtos Beach – prosciutto, local cheeses, olives, village bread, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Harbourside fine dining in Fiskardo – lobster pasta (a Kefalonian specialty), grilled red mullet, and a bottle of Gentilini Robola white wine

day_by_day.notes: The speedboat transfer between islands must be pre-booked through a specialist maritime charter company. Confirm sea conditions the day before. Myrtos Beach has no facilities so all supplies must come from the boat. Fiskardo accommodation should be pre-booked well in advance as it is extremely popular in June.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Melissani Cave – a stunning underground lake where sunlight filters through a collapsed roof to illuminate the turquoise water in otherworldly colors. Arrive early (before 9:30) to avoid crowds. Follow with a visit to the Drogarati stalactite cave nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south by private car to the Lixouri peninsula. Visit the red-sand beach of Xi Beach for a swim and relaxation. Stop at a local ceramics workshop in Lixouri town for a private demonstration and shopping. Return north via the scenic mountain road through Ainos National Park.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a clifftop bar above Assos village, a beautifully preserved Venetian settlement on a tiny peninsula. Dinner at an acclaimed restaurant in Assos with views of the castle-crowned headland.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Fiskardo – eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh pastries, fruit, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional taverna in Lixouri – Kefalonian meat pie (kreatopita), horta (wild greens), grilled fish, and local wine
meals.dinner: Assos village restaurant – pan-seared sea bass, wild mushroom risotto, and local Kefalonian Muscat dessert wine with a walnut tart

day_by_day.notes: Melissani Cave is extremely popular – early arrival is essential. The drive through Ainos National Park offers spectacular views of the Ionian Sea on both sides of the island. A private driver is recommended for the full day to allow flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning in Fiskardo. Enjoy a slow breakfast at the harbor café, browse the boutique shops, and take a kayaking or paddleboarding session in the calm bay. Optional: visit the small Roman cemetery ruins and the Byzantine lighthouse on the headland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat transfer from Kefalonia to Lefkada island (approximately 2 hours via the Ionian Sea). Check into a luxury villa or boutique hotel near Porto Katsiki or Egremni Beach on the west coast. These are among the most spectacular beaches in all of Greece.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Lefkada – sunset walk along the dramatic white cliffs above Porto Katsiki. Dinner at a stylish restaurant in Vasiliki village at the southern tip of the island.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Fiskardo harbor – fresh croissants, Greek yogurt, local honey, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the boat during the transfer – charcuterie, fresh fruit, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Vasiliki village restaurant – fresh catch of the day, garlic shrimp, Greek village salad, and a carafe of local white wine

day_by_day.notes: The speedboat transfer to Lefkada is an open-sea crossing and conditions can vary. Confirm with the charter company the morning of departure. Lefkada is technically connected to mainland Greece by a floating bridge, but the boat approach to the west coast beaches is the most dramatic. Villa check-in should be pre-arranged.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at Porto Katsiki Beach – widely considered one of the most beautiful beaches in Europe. The 150-meter white pebble beach sits beneath towering white chalk cliffs. Access via a private boat is the premium way to arrive, bypassing the staircase crowds. Swim, snorkel, and sunbathe in complete luxury.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat hop to Egremni Beach (accessible only by sea or a very long staircase), an even more secluded stretch of white pebbles and deep blue water. Anchor offshore and spend the afternoon in total seclusion. The boat captain can prepare fresh grilled fish onboard.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the villa for a rest and freshen up. Drive to Lefkada Town for an evening stroll along the charming waterfront promenade lined with colorful Venetian-influenced wooden buildings. Dinner at a renowned restaurant on the main square.

meals.breakfast: Villa breakfast – Greek yogurt with local honey and walnuts, fresh fruit, eggs, village bread, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Freshly grilled fish and vegetables prepared by the boat captain onboard, with chilled Assyrtiko wine
meals.dinner: Lefkada Town restaurant – slow-cooked lamb with orzo (giouvetsi), cheese saganaki, and a bottle of Agiorgitiko red wine

day_by_day.notes: Porto Katsiki and Egremni are best visited on weekdays if possible as weekend crowds increase significantly in June. The boat is the only truly premium way to experience both beaches. Bring plenty of water and sun protection as shade is minimal.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Lefkada interior – visit the mountain villages of Karya and Englouvi, famous for their lace embroidery and lentil cultivation. Meet local artisans and learn about traditional crafts. Sample local produce including the renowned Englouvi lentils, local honey, and tsipouro spirit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the beautiful east coast of Lefkada – explore the calm, turquoise lagoon beaches of Nydri Bay and the offshore islands. Take a short boat ride to Skorpios Island (formerly owned by Aristotle Onassis) and sail around its perimeter admiring the lush private estate from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar near Agios Nikitas, a charming fishing village on the northwest coast. Dinner at the village's best seafood taverna right on the water's edge.

meals.breakfast: Villa breakfast – full Greek spread with pastries, cold cuts, local cheeses, tomatoes, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Traditional mountain lunch in Karya village – bean soup (fasolada), stuffed peppers, local sausages, and barrel wine
meals.dinner: Agios Nikitas waterfront taverna – grilled octopus, sea urchin pasta, fresh catch of the day, and chilled local rosé

day_by_day.notes: The mountain villages are noticeably cooler than the coast – bring a light layer. Skorpios Island is private property; circumnavigation by boat is permitted but landing is not. The Agios Nikitas taverna is very popular – ask the villa manager to make a reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Private yacht charter for a full-day sailing excursion around the Lefkada archipelago. Depart from Nydri marina and sail to the uninhabited islands of Meganisi, Kalamos, and Kastos. Swim in hidden coves accessible only by sea, snorkel over Posidonia seagrass meadows, and enjoy the complete freedom of the open Ionian.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue sailing south toward the island of Meganisi. Anchor in the stunning natural harbor of Vathy or Spartochori village. Explore the tiny village on foot, visit the local bakery, and enjoy an afternoon swim off the boat's stern platform.
day_by_day.evening: Sail back to Nydri as the sun sets over the Ionian. Dinner at a premium restaurant in Nydri with views of the illuminated islands. This is the final evening in Lefkada.

meals.breakfast: Villa breakfast – smoked salmon and cream cheese bagels, fresh fruit, and Greek coffee before departure
meals.lunch: Catered gourmet lunch onboard the yacht – Greek meze spread, fresh seafood, and premium chilled wines
meals.dinner: Nydri marina restaurant – grilled jumbo prawns, black ink risotto, and a bottle of Domaine Sigalas Santorini white wine

day_by_day.notes: Full-day yacht charters in the Lefkada archipelago should be booked at least 1 week in advance, especially in peak June season. Confirm whether a skipper and hostess are included. Bring motion sickness tablets if needed. Pack a light windbreaker as it can be breezy on open water.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Lefkada to Preveza Airport or Aktion Airport (approximately 1 hour drive). Short domestic flight or private charter to Athens. Check into a 5-star luxury hotel in Athens (Syntagma or Kolonaki area). Freshen up and begin exploring the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the Acropolis and Parthenon with a licensed archaeologist guide. Visit early enough to beat the afternoon heat. Follow with a walk through the Plaka neighborhood – Athens' oldest district – browsing boutique shops and artisan galleries. Visit the New Acropolis Museum for an air-conditioned cultural immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop cocktails at a luxury hotel bar with iconic Acropolis views as the ancient monument is dramatically lit. Dinner at one of Athens' most celebrated fine dining restaurants in Kolonaki.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at Lefkada villa before departure – pastries, fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Upscale lunch restaurant in Plaka – modern Greek cuisine, grilled vegetables, lamb chops, and a glass of Naoussa Xinomavro red wine
meals.dinner: Fine dining in Kolonaki – tasting menu featuring modern interpretations of ancient Greek recipes, paired with a curated Greek wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Acropolis tickets online well in advance to skip queues – timed entry slots sell out quickly in June. The private archaeologist guide dramatically enhances the experience. Athens can be very hot in the afternoon – schedule the Acropolis visit for 9:00–11:00 or after 17:00.

day_by_day.morning: Private food tour of Athens' Central Market (Varvakios Agora) with a local food journalist or chef guide. Explore the aromatic stalls of fresh fish, hanging meats, spices, olives, and cheeses. Sample local delicacies including fresh loukoumades (honey doughnuts), taramosalata, and artisan cheeses. Visit a specialty Greek coffee roaster.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood – browse high-end boutiques, visit the Benaki Museum of Greek Culture, and enjoy a leisurely afternoon at a stylish café on Tsakalof Street. Optional: visit the National Archaeological Museum for an unparalleled collection of ancient Greek artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar in Monastiraki with sweeping Acropolis views. Farewell dinner at an acclaimed Athens restaurant – a celebration of the entire trip.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – lavish buffet with every Greek specialty, fresh juices, and espresso
meals.lunch: Upscale mezedopoleio (meze restaurant) in the Central Market area – a feast of small plates: taramosalata, grilled halloumi, spanakopita, lamb meatballs, and house wine
meals.dinner: Celebrated Athens fine dining restaurant – chef's tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring dishes like sea urchin with Cretan olive oil, slow-roasted suckling pig, and Greek cheese selection

day_by_day.notes: The Varvakios market is most vibrant in the morning (8:00–11:00). The food tour lasts approximately 3 hours. The Benaki Museum has an excellent rooftop café worth visiting even without the full museum tour. Make dinner reservations at least 3–4 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Athens. Enjoy a long breakfast at the hotel. Take a final stroll through the Zappeion Gardens or along the elegant Dionysiou Areopagitou pedestrian promenade at the base of the Acropolis. Visit any last-minute boutique shops for premium Greek souvenirs – extra virgin olive oil, saffron, mastiha liqueur, and artisan ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, enjoy a final Greek lunch at a rooftop restaurant with Acropolis views. Private transfer to Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos). Check in for departure flight. Relax in the premium lounge before boarding.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry the flavors, memories, and warmth of the Ionian Islands and Athens home.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast – full Greek spread enjoyed slowly with no rush
meals.lunch: Rooftop restaurant near the Acropolis – light farewell meal of grilled fish, Greek salad, tzatziki, and a final glass of chilled Assyrtiko
meals.dinner: Airport premium lounge or in-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for Athens airport check-in, especially in peak summer season. Pre-book a private airport transfer. Consider purchasing a premium Greek food hamper from a specialty deli near the hotel to take home – Attica department store in Syntagma has an excellent gourmet food hall. Confirm all hotel checkouts and transfer times the evening before.
